description.narrative:
ltpgt
lt/pgtltp class="" style=""gtltspan style="font-family:"gtUNICEF’s proposed project will provide integrated life-saving comprehensive packages of services to at least 55,000 vulnerable populations, including 5,700 under-five children, 2200 pregnant and lactating women, and 500 persons with disabilities, their caregivers and communities in need in 7 townships in Bago East area, which rated high priority in the HRP 2023, are severally impacted by conflict, and deprived of life-saving and essential services. UNICEF will work with its non-government partners, including local organizations and faith and young groups, to reach children, care givers, and their communities affected by conflict with an integrated package of life-saving interventions, which include: ltbrgt ltbrgt lt/spangtlt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom:9.95pt"gtltbgtltspan style="font-family:"gtNutrition: lt/spangtlt/bgtltspan style="font-family:"gtprovision of life-saving preventive and curative nutrition services, including nutrition screening and treatment of children with acute malnutrition, maternal infant and young child feeding (MIYCF) counselling, and multiple micro-nutrient supplementations to children and pregnant lactation women coordination as a sector lead of the nutrition cluster and provision of supplies to scale up services. ltbrgtltbrgtlt/spangtltb style="font-size: 14px"gtHealth: lt/bgtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gtDelivery of essential life-saving packages of maternal, newborn, and child health care outreach extension/mobile health team approach home-based care at the community level by trained community-based health volunteers referral of emergency/high-risk cases and capacity building of health care providers to deliver primary health care services and to identify emergency/high-risk cases for referral as per national and global recommendations. lt/spangtltspan style="font-family:"gtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltp class="" style=""gtltspan style="color: black font-family: Arial, sans-serif"gtUNICEF will integrate prevention and mitigation of GBV and PSEA and refer the victims to appropriate services. Social and Behavior Change programme (SBC) and accountability to the affected population (AAP) interventions will establish platforms to seek feedback and sensitize the targeted communities. lt/spangtltspan style="font-family:"gtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltp class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom:9.95pt"gtltspan style="color: black font-family: Arial, sans-serif"gtltbrgtIn Myanmar, SBC has spearheaded innovative platforms to develop and deliver messaging to affected populations through innovative digital media, such as Viber Knowledge Talk channel, creative IEC materials, and SBC and IPC training for community-based volunteers. These approaches have helped reach over 2 million people in development and humanitarian settings in the past year.lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltp class="" style=""gtSBC in UNICEF also spearheads the AAP interventions to give communities a platform to give feedback and participate in decisions around services that affect their lives. This community feedback mechanism and response approach has informed the planning of programme service sectors to design /redesign their services for the communities. This includes interventions such as setting up of AAP dashboard for partners to log in feedback from communities, AAP e-course in local Myanmar language accessible all over the country, including hard-to-reach areas, and training of partners on AAP approaches and feedback mechanisms. ltbrgtlt/pgtltp class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom:9.95pt"gtltspan style="font-family:"gtltbrgtlt/spangtltspan style="color: black font-family: Arial, sans-serif"gtThe proposed project will complement UNICEF’s ongoing support for humanitarian response and scale up nutrition and health services through partners to have timely responses and ensure the availability of critical social services in those areas.lt/spangtlt/pgtltp class="sceditor-nlf"gtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtlt/pgt
